title: Violent or Graphic Content
summary: YouTube does not permit violent or gory content that's intended to be shocking, sensational, or disrespectful.
prohibited: Inciting violence against individuals or groups
Footage of physical fights involving minors
Graphic depictions of road accidents, dead bodies, or severe injuries without educational context
Animal abuse or cruelty staged for entertainment
exceptions: Educational, Documentary, Scientific, or Artistic (EDSA) context, provided clear warnings, blurring, or educational narration is present.
monetization_impact: Yellow Dollar or Complete Demonetization + Age Restriction
remediation: Blur graphic sections, remove sensational sound effects over injuries, add educational commentary or content warnings in intro.

title: Harassment and Cyberbullying
summary: Content that targets an individual with prolonged insults, racial/sexual slurs, doxxing, or malicious attacks is strictly prohibited.
prohibited: Revealing someone's private personal information (doxxing phone numbers, addresses)
Targeted harassment based on protected attributes (race, gender, sexual orientation)
Encouraging an audience to abuse, harass, or brigade another channel
Malicious insults or dehumanizing comparisons
exceptions: Public interest commentary, satire, or debates between public figures, so long as it does not cross into targeted abuse or personal threats.
remediation: Censor personal identifying information, rephrase harsh personal accusations to focus on ideas/actions, remove aggressive call-to-actions.

title: Misinformation & Harmful Conspiracy
summary: Content that misleads viewers and poses a serious risk of egregious real-world harm is forbidden.
prohibited: Medical advice that contradicts local health authorities or WHO (e.g., miracle cures for fatal diseases)
Voter suppression or false claims regarding election procedures and dates
Denial of violent historical events or atrocities
exceptions: Reporting on misconceptions with clear fact-checking debunking, artistic parody with prominent satire disclaimers.
remediation: Cite accredited scientific sources or peer-reviewed journals, frame discussions as exploratory reporting, add disclaimers.

title: Harmful or Dangerous Acts & Challenges
summary: Content that encourages dangerous or illegal activities that risk serious physical harm or death.
prohibited: Extremely dangerous challenges with risk of injury or death
Pranks that lead victims to fear imminent physical harm or emotional trauma
Instructions for creating homemade explosives or modifying firearms
Promoting hard drug use or dangerous prescription abuse
exceptions: Professional stunt performers with visible safety apparatus and prominent disclaimers ('Do not attempt at home').
remediation: Include visible disclaimer banner, do not provide step-by-step instructions for dangerous behaviors, emphasize professional supervision.

title: Content ID Matching & Audio Fingerprinting
summary: YouTube automatically scans all uploads against a vast database of copyrighted audio and video recordings owned by labels and studios.
prohibited: Using commercial music tracks without a sync/master license (even if credited or under 10 seconds)
Uploading full movie clips, sports broadcasts, or music videos
Cover songs without mechanical rights or ad-revenue sharing agreements
exceptions: YouTube Audio Library (royalty-free), Creative Commons Attribution (CC-BY), or licensed royalty-free libraries (Epidemic Sound, Artlist).
monetization_impact: Content ID Claim: 100% Ad Revenue diverted to copyright owner
remediation: Replace commercial audio with copyright-safe background music, use YouTube Audio Library, or license through an official service.

title: Fair Use Doctrine (4-Factor Test)
summary: Fair use is a legal doctrine in the US permitting unlicensed use of copyrighted material in certain circumstances such as criticism, commentary, news reporting, teaching, or research.
prohibited: Mere re-uploading with minimal commentary (e.g. silent reaction videos)
Using substantial portions of the original work that diminish the commercial market for the original
Relying on disclaimers like 'No copyright infringement intended' (legally ineffective)
exceptions: Highly transformative works where the original clip is strictly used to illustrate a specific critical point, parody, or educational analysis.
monetization_impact: Risk of manual copyright strike if owner disagrees with fair use defense
remediation: Keep clip excerpts under 5-10 seconds, speak directly over the clip, add on-screen annotations, zoom or transform visually, provide original critical perspective.

title: Inappropriate Language & Profanity Rules
summary: YouTube strictly monitors swearing and strong profanity, especially in the opening seconds and metadata.
prohibited: Strong profanity (e.g., the F-word or explicit sexual curse words) in the first 7-8 seconds of the video
Vulgar or profanity-laden video titles and custom thumbnails
Continuous, pervasive profanity throughout the entire video
exceptions: Moderate language (damn, hell, crap) used casually after the first 8 seconds usually qualifies for full monetization.
remediation: Bleep or mute strong expletives during the first 10 seconds; keep titles and thumbnails 100% G-rated for broad advertiser appeal.

title: Sensationalism & Deceptive Metadata
summary: Misleading titles, deceitful thumbnails, or exaggerated claims designed solely to manipulate clicks without delivering the payoff.
prohibited: Thumbnails featuring shocking imagery that never occurs in the video
Titles making factual promises that are completely refuted or ignored in the video
Stuffing irrelevant tags in the video description (against YouTube TOS)
exceptions: Dramatic curiosity hooks that are genuinely resolved and fulfilled inside the video narrative.
monetization_impact: Reduced algorithmic distribution, shadow-demotion, or viewer refund flags
remediation: Ensure the promise in the thumbnail and title is paid off within the first 60 seconds; do not put comma-separated tag blocks inside descriptions.

title: Reused Content & Repetitive Shorts
summary: YouTube Partner Program (YPP) strictly requires original value. Uploading aggregated compilations or mass-reposted clips from TikTok/Instagram without transformative editing will cause monetization refusal.
prohibited: Raw screen recordings of other creators' Shorts or TikToks
Mass automated AI voiceovers reading generic Reddit threads with unrelated gameplay background
Unmodified podcast clips uploaded without added commentary or narrative editing
exceptions: Curated commentary, multi-angle analysis, motion graphics, and unique value-add narration.
remediation: Add an on-screen face/avatar, personal perspective voiceover, dynamic zoom/crop cuts, custom animations and original graphic overlays.
